name: Nose exercises (nose yoga)

card.summary: Nostril flaring and nose scrunching routines claimed to reshape the nose; no studies have tested them.

quick.overview:
Nose exercises are muscle routines such as nostril flaring that proponents say can slim the nostrils or lift the tip.

No published studies were found on whether they change nose shape.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say exercising the small muscles around the nose changes its shape. The nose's main structure is bone and cartilage, which these muscles do not directly reshape.
quick.risks: No documented harms specific to the practice were found.

lead: Nose exercises, often called nose yoga, are routines of flaring the nostrils, scrunching or wiggling the nose, lifting the tip or pinching the nose while breathing, promoted as a free, non-surgical way to slim the nostrils, sharpen the tip or make the nose look more refined. They belong to the wider category of facial exercise or face yoga, and circulate in beauty articles and short-form video.[2]

People who try them aim to tone the small muscles around the nose, on the idea that stronger or differently-held muscles will change how the nostrils and tip sit. One of these muscles, the depressor septi nasi, pulls the nasal tip and the base of the nostrils downward and moves the tip when the upper lip moves, which is the anatomical basis proponents point to for tip-lifting routines.[1]

Healthline, in its overview of the practice, states that the base of the nose is shaped by bone and the tip by cartilage, and that no scientific evidence shows the exercises change nose shape; it lists contouring makeup, dermal filler and rhinoplasty as alternatives.[2] No clinical studies of nose exercises have been found.

chain: Repeated flaring, scrunching or tip-lifting works the small muscles around the nose
Proponents expect a slimmer nostril base or lifted tip
angle.text: Practitioners do the routines daily in the hope of a narrower, sharper-looking nose without surgery or filler. The movements involve the muscles around the nostrils and tip, such as the depressor septi nasi.

infobox: Slimmer nostrils, lifted tip, sharper nose

paras: Routines described by proponents involve repeatedly flaring, lifting or compressing the nose using the small muscles around it. A commonly shared example pairs pinching the nose with flaring the nostrils.[2] The depressor septi nasi, one of these muscles, pulls the nasal tip and nostril base downward and also moves the nasal tip when the upper lip moves.[1]

Healthline describes nose exercises as a popular internet trend and states that there is no scientific evidence that they work, noting that nasal shape is determined mainly by bone and cartilage rather than by the small muscles the routines target.[2] The same article lists contouring makeup, which changes the appearance of the nose without changing its size, dermal filler (non-surgical rhinoplasty, lasting roughly six months), rhinoplasty and septoplasty as the established ways of changing appearance or breathing.[2]
